The announcement of the 2008 [Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences") in Nobel Prize Press Conference. The laureate of the Prize was [Paul Krugman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Krugman "Paul Krugman").

The **Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences**, officially the **Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of [Alfred Nobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel")**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-3) ([Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_language "Swedish language"): _Sveriges riksbanks pris i ekonomisk vetenskap till Alfred Nobels minne_), commonly referred to as the **Nobel Prize in Economics**, is an award in the field of [Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_Sciences "Economic Sciences") administered by the [Nobel Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-NobelPrizeSelectionProcess-4)

The first Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded in 1969 to [Ragnar Frisch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ragnar_Frisch "Ragnar Frisch") and [Jan Tinbergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Tinbergen "Jan Tinbergen").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-Winners1969-5) Each recipient receives a [medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medal "Medal"), a [diploma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploma "Diploma") and a monetary award that has varied throughout the years.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-NobelPrizeDescription-6) In 1969, Frisch and Tinbergen were given a combined 375,000 [SEK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_krona "Swedish krona"), which is equivalent to 2,871,041 SEK in December 2007. The award is presented in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm") at an annual ceremony on December 10, the anniversary of Nobel's death.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-7)

As of the awarding of the 2023 prize, 55 Prizes in Economic Sciences have been given to 93 individuals.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-NobelLaureatesList-8) As of October 2023, the department of economics with the most affiliated [laureates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laureate "Laureate") in economic sciences is the [University of Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago "University of Chicago"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economic_Sciences#cite_note-10) with 16 affiliated laureates. As of 2023, the institutions with the most [PhD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Philosophy "Doctor of Philosophy") (or equivalent) graduates who went on to receive the prize are Harvard University and MIT (13 each), followed by the University of Chicago (10). As of 2024, the institutions with the most affiliated faculty at the time of the award are the University of Chicago (15), followed by MIT (10), then by Princeton University and Harvard University (8 each).
